body:
Fixes #2263

## Summary

- treat a diagnostic-rich terminal Claude tool failure as execution failure even when the provider emits a top-level success envelope; a later successful tool result still supersedes an earlier exploratory failure
- keep the established critical-error recovery behavior: auto-commit and best-effort push every Git-visible change, with generated artifacts controlled only by the repository's `.gitignore`
- restore and deliberately retain draft state after tool failures, exceptions, restart exhaustion, and no-progress termination
- prevent session teardown and both auto-merge paths from overriding a failure draft
- require restart iterations to report actual success, no execution error, and a non-empty PR before restoring ready-for-review state
- refresh the reproducible Agent CLI image pin to 0.26.5 after the live dependency-freshness gate detected the newly published release

## Root cause

The Formal AI stream contained a detailed failed `javac` tool result, followed by a provider-level `success` event. Hive Mind retained the tool diagnostic but still classified the overall session as successful. Recovery then auto-committed the dirty tree; because that left no pending changes and the target repository had no CI, later cleanup treated the recovery commit as a verified solution and marked the PR ready before publishing the terminal failure.

## Recovery policy

Recovery commits remain intentional evidence and are still pushed to the PR branch. Hive Mind does not guess which file extensions are disposable:

- when the repository ignores `*.class`, `Main.class` is excluded by Git
- without that ignore rule, `Main.class` is preserved with the other recovery changes

In either case, a failed or unverified session remains a draft and cannot be reported as ready or auto-merged during the run. A later fresh working session may repair the recovery commit and earn readiness through a real successful result.

## Regression coverage

`tests/failed-recovery-stays-draft-2263.test.mjs` now:

- replays the reported failed-`javac`/provider-success ordering through the real Claude command wrapper and verifies a failed result with retained compiler diagnostics
- uses real temporary Git repositories and a bare remote to verify recovery commit/push behavior
- verifies `.gitignore` excludes compiler output, while an unignored artifact is committed
- reproduces the clean-worktree/no-CI readiness attempt and verifies the failure draft veto
- checks no-progress and both auto-merge paths retain the failure ordering

## Verification

- `npm test` — all 494 selected test files pass
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `npm run check:secrets`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs` — all 148 declarations current
- `HIVE_MIND_FORMAL_AI_PATH=/nonexistent/formal-ai node tests/failed-recovery-stays-draft-2263.test.mjs` — passes without an installed Formal AI runtime

This is a non-UI recovery/state-management change, so screenshots are not applicable.
title: fix(solve): keep failed recovered sessions in draft

body:
## Problem

Issue #2169: a `/solve` run burned **3 h 55 min** and **$7.65** and then died with

```
❌ Transient API error persisted after 10 retries
```

The captured log ([`docs/case-studies/issue-2169/data/run.log.txt`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2169-27fa2d8703d4/docs/case-studies/issue-2169/data/run.log.txt), 30,806 lines) shows the run **never hit a single API error**: all 11 Claude invocations ended `"subtype": "success"`, `"is_error": false`, `"api_error_status": null`. What the retry loop called a "Gateway error (502/504/52x)" was the agent's own success summary — the work was on `hybrid-Intelligence-lab` **issue #523 / PR #524**, and the classifier tested the text with a bare `/\b52[0-4]\b/`.

Three lines apart in the log:

```
✅ Stream closed normally after result event
⚠️ Gateway error (502/504/52x) detected. Retry 1/10 in 2 min (session preserved)...
   Error: Готово. PR: https://github.com/G-Ivan-A/hybrid-Intelligence-lab/pull/524 (ready for review, …)
```

## Root causes

| #   | Root cause                                                                                                                         | Fix                                                                                                              |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| RC1 | `classifyRetryableError` matched **any** standalone `520`–`524` in the message — PR numbers, issue numbers, line numbers            | New `matchesHttpStatus()`: a status code counts only next to an error context (`API Error: 502`, `error code: 522`, `HTTP 504`) or a canonical gateway phrase. Applied to the gateway and 503 branches. |
| RC2 | `claude.lib.mjs` ran the transient-error gate **even when the run had succeeded** (`subtype: success`, exit 0)                      | `runProducedSuccess` gate — a successful run is never retried; the near-miss is logged in verbose mode so a future misclassification is diagnosable from the log alone. |
| RC3 | 10 attempts × 2 → 30 min ≈ **3.5 h** implicit ceiling — too short for a real provider outage (the issue's own requirement)          | Wall-clock **retry budget**: 12 h by default, configurable, 3-minute minimum delay, `3 → 30` min backoff; the attempt count is demoted to a runaway backstop. |

## What changed

- **`src/tool-retry.lib.mjs`** — `matchesHttpStatus()`, `formatRetryDuration()`, `createTransientRetryBudget()` (`evaluate` / `grant` / `describeProgress` / `describeExhaustion`), and `describeClassificationEvidence()`.
- **Diagnosable logging** — the old retry line printed only `lastMessage.substring(0, 200)`, so the `PR #524` token that fired the classifier (1.6 KB into the message) never appeared in the reported log. Under `--verbose`, `claude.lib.mjs` now also logs `Classification evidence: label="…" messageChars=1783 statusTokens=[@1642 "…Opened PR #524 for the fix…"]` on both the retry path and the new success near-miss path.
- **`src/config.lib.mjs`** — new/updated, all env-overridable:

  | Env var                                      | Default            | Meaning                                        |
  | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
  | `HIVE_MIND_TRANSIENT_ERROR_RETRY_BUDGET_MS`  | `43200000` (12 h)  | Total retry window; `0` = unlimited            |
  | `HIVE_MIND_MIN_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS`     | `180000` (3 min)   | Floor for every transient wait                 |
  | `HIVE_MIND_INITIAL_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS` | `180000` (3 min)   | First backoff step                             |
  | `HIVE_MIND_MAX_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS`     | `1800000` (30 min) | Backoff ceiling                                |
  | `HIVE_MIND_MAX_TRANSIENT_ERROR_RETRIES`      | `100`              | Runaway backstop                               |

- **Applied across the whole codebase** (issue requirement): `claude`, `agent`, `gemini`, `qwen`, `codex` (both retry blocks), `opencode`, and `claude.connection.lib.mjs` — the last one previously had its own `maxRetries = 3` and now shares the budget through a single `retryAfterOverload()` helper. RC2 was verified to be claude-specific; the other tools already gate their retry blocks behind an explicit failure condition.
- **`docs/case-studies/issue-2169/`** — full run log, decisive excerpts, issue data, research sources, and a deep analysis (timeline, root causes, solution plans, library survey, requirements checklist).
- **`.changeset/transient-retry-budget-2169.md`** — patch release.

## How to reproduce and verify

Reproduce the root cause against the real log:

```console
$ node experiments/issue-2169-replay-log-classification.mjs
attempt  1: old=RETRY new=ok    52x-hits=["524"] :: Готово. PR: …/pull/524…
…
payloads: 11
classified retryable by OLD matcher: 11
classified retryable by NEW matcher: 0
```

Automated tests — `tests/transient-retry-budget-2169.test.mjs` (27 assertions):

- each captured success summary is **not** retryable;
- `502 Bad Gateway`, `520 Unknown Error`, `523 Origin Is Unreachable`, `api error: 503`, `status code: 503`, `504 Gateway Timeout` are still retryable;
- **end-to-end regression**: `executeClaudeCommand` fed one `result/success` event containing `pull/524` invokes the CLI exactly once, returns `success: true`, and emits neither `Retry attempt` nor `Transient API error persisted`;
- budget behaviour: defaults, 3-min floor, floor clamped by max, a simulated 12-hour outage (injected clock) granting >20 retries over 11–12 h ending with `reason: 'budget'`, the `3, 6, 12, 24, 30` min schedule, a shorter configurable budget, the count backstop, `budgetMs = 0` → unlimited, and `formatRetryDuration` rendering.

`tests/test-internal-server-error-retry.mjs` and `tests/test-request-timeout-retry.mjs` were updated to the new defaults. **All 406 test files pass** locally (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, exit 0) and `npm run lint` is clean.

## Upstream reporting

Investigated as the issue requires: **no upstream defect**. The log has zero non-null `api_error_status` values and eleven `subtype: success` results — the Anthropic API and the Claude CLI behaved correctly; the failure was entirely ours. Details and the related existing upstream threads are in the case study.

## Requirements checklist

All 11 requirements extracted from the issue are tracked in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2169/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2169-27fa2d8703d4/docs/case-studies/issue-2169/README.md#requirements-checklist) — every one is ✅.

Fixes #2169
title: fix(retry): stop retrying successful runs and give transient API errors a 12-hour budget (#2169)

body:
Fixes #2168.

## What happened

A `solve` run cloned `ideav/crm`, created and pushed the branch, confirmed via the compare API that it was one commit ahead of `main` — and then died **3.1 seconds later** on the next command:

```
19:28:11.478  gh pr create --draft … --head issue-4804-203a323f30b1 --repo ideav/crm
19:28:14.595  ❌ FATAL ERROR: PR creation failed: GraphQL: Something went wrong while
              executing your query on 2026-08-21T19:28:14Z. Please include
              `811E:19A5B0:3A5AA9:37C97F:6A88A6CC` when reporting this issue.
```

3.1 s is less than the first backoff delay of the day (1 s + 2 s over 3 attempts): **zero retries happened**, even though the call was already routed through the retry wrapper added in #1756.

## Root cause

GitHub does not use HTTP status codes to report internal GraphQL failures — per the GraphQL spec it answers **`200 OK`** and puts the fault in an `errors[]` payload. The transient classifier keyed exclusively on transport faults and the literal strings `http 502` / `http 503` / `http 504`, so `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query …` matched nothing, was classified permanent, and aborted the session at `src/solve.auto-pr.lib.mjs:1281`.

Contributing causes: the pattern vocabulary was duplicated in two modules and had drifted; the transient budget reused `maxApiRetries` (3 s total); nothing logged *why* an error was not retried and GitHub's support reference id was discarded; ~36 network-facing **git** call sites had no retry at all; and making 5xx retryable creates a double-write hazard for `gh pr create`.

Full analysis, timeline, prior-art survey and per-requirement solution plan: [`docs/case-studies/issue-2168/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2168-db984f30a3e9/docs/case-studies/issue-2168).

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/transient-errors.lib.mjs` | **new** — one source of truth for transient classification, now including the GraphQL 200-with-`errors[]` family, plus diagnostics and support-reference-id extraction |
| `src/git-retry.lib.mjs` | **new** — `matchGitNetworkCommand`, `wrapDollarWithGitRetry` |
| `src/github-pr-idempotency.lib.mjs` | **new** — recover the existing PR URL when a retry hits "a pull request already exists" |
| `src/github-rate-limit.lib.mjs` | classification delegated to the shared module; non-`gh` git network commands routed through `gitCmdRetry` |
| `src/lib.mjs` | `gitCmdRetry` gained transient classification, diagnostics and an injectable `log` |
| `src/config.lib.mjs` | `maxGitHubTransientRetries` (6), `initialGitHubTransientDelayMs` (2000), `maxGitRetries` (5) + env overrides |
| `src/solve.auto-pr.lib.mjs` | both `gh pr create` sites go through the idempotent `runPrCreate()` |
| `src/{agent,codex,gemini,qwen,opencode}.lib.mjs` | module-level `$` wrapped with `wrapDollarWithGitRetry` |
| `eslint-rules/no-unretried-git-network.mjs` + `eslint.config.mjs` | **new rule**, scoped to `src/**` |

**Coverage without touching 36 call sites.** The retry is installed on command-stream's `` $ `` **tag** — the pattern already used by `wrapDollarWithGhRetry` — and `src/solve.mjs` passes that wrapped `` $ `` down to every helper module, so all downstream git calls inherit it and new call sites are covered by construction. `git clone` is deliberately excluded: a partially written destination makes attempt #2 fail with *"already exists and is not an empty directory"*.

**Better logging (issue requirement).** Every non-retry decision now emits a verbose line naming the classification, the matched pattern, the attempt counter and the exit code, and `parseGitHubRequestId()` captures both the `811E:…` support reference and `X-GitHub-Request-Id` — so the next occurrence is diagnosable from the log alone and reportable to GitHub support.

## How to reproduce

```
node experiments/issue-2168-smoke.mjs
```

The smoke script drives a fake `` $ `` that returns the verbatim message from the issue title. Before the fix it is classified non-transient and the wrapper performs exactly one attempt; after the fix it is classified as a GitHub server error and the wrapper retries up to `maxGitHubTransientRetries`.

## Tests

- `tests/transient-retry-2168.test.mjs` — **19 passed, 0 failed**: transient classification (7, asserting on the verbatim issue message), gh retry (2), git network command detection (2), git retry (5), `gh pr create` idempotency (3).
- `tests/test-no-unretried-git-network-rule.mjs` — ESLint `RuleTester`, 10 valid + 4 invalid cases.
- `experiments/issue-2168-smoke.mjs` — end-to-end smoke over the wrapper chain.
- `npm run lint` — clean with the new rule enabled across `src/**`.

## Upstream

The gap is also `gh`'s: it surfaces GraphQL 200-with-`errors[]` as a bare non-zero exit with no retry and no machine-readable reference id. That is already open upstream as [cli/cli#13432](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/13432) (*"No partial result, no retry behavior surfaced by the CLI"*), alongside [#7735](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/7735) and [#4037](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4037). Rather than file a duplicate, the reproducible evidence from this incident — command, reference id, the 3.1 s no-retry window, the workaround, and the suggested fix — is compiled in §4 and §5 (R6) of the case study, ready to attach to the existing thread.
title: fix(retry): retry transient GitHub GraphQL and git network failures (#2168)

body:
## Summary

Fixes #1935 — a regression from PR #1924.

A long-running solve session (588 turns, ~$70.62) hit Claude's **5-hour session limit**. The Claude CLI reported it as a `result` event with `api_error_status: 429` and:

```
You've hit your session limit · resets 4pm (UTC)
```

Instead of being handled as an **account usage limit** (post a comment with the reset time + wait until the exact reset moment), it was put through the **transient** exponential-backoff retry loop:

```
⚠️ Server rate limited (429) detected. Retry 1/10 in 2 min (session preserved)...
   Error: You've hit your session limit · resets 4pm (UTC)
⚠️ Server rate limited (429) detected. Retry 2/10 in 4 min (session preserved)...
```

Each retry re-hit the same limit (the quota only frees at the reset time), so the harness burned ~10 futile retries **and never told the user when the limit resets**.

## Root cause (blame: PR #1924, commit `24fb17ed`)

`src/claude.lib.mjs` set `isRateLimitError = true` for **every** structured `api_error_status === 429`, without checking whether the message was an account usage limit. Claude reports **both** conditions with `api_error_status: 429`:

| Condition | Example message | Correct handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transient throttle (#1924) | `Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit) · Rate limited` | retry with `--resume` after a short backoff |
| Account usage limit (#1935) | `You've hit your session limit · resets 4pm (UTC)` | post a comment + wait until the **exact reset time** |

#1924 narrowed the *text* classifier (`classifyRetryableError`) correctly, but the *structured* 429 check it added bypassed that narrowing and swept genuine usage limits into the transient-retry path — ahead of `detectUsageLimit()`, which was therefore never reached.

## The fix

- **`src/claude.lib.mjs`** — only flag a structured 429 as a transient rate limit when the message is **not** a usage limit:
  ```js
  if (data.api_error_status === 429 && !isUsageLimitError(lastMessage)) { ... }
  ```
  Session/weekly limits now fall through to the usage-limit handler, which immediately posts a comment and (with `--auto-continue-limit`) waits until the exact reset moment and auto-resumes.
- **`src/usage-limit.lib.mjs`** — recognise the `"hit your session limit"` / `"hit your weekly limit"` phrasing as a backstop (the `"resets 4pm"` regex already matched).

**Codebase coverage:** `claude.lib.mjs` is the only site that special-cases a structured 429. Every other tool wrapper (codex, gemini, opencode, qwen, agent) routes errors through the shared `classifyRetryableError` text classifier, which was already narrow and never matched account usage limits — so no change is needed there.

## How to reproduce

Feed the harness a Claude `result` event with `is_error: true`, `api_error_status: 429`, and `result: "You've hit your session limit · resets 4pm (UTC)"`. Before the fix it logs `Retry 1/10 in 2 min`; after the fix it routes to the usage-limit reset-time wait. The captured real-world log is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-1935/data/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-1935-c4011ebdc787/docs/case-studies/issue-1935).

## Tests

`tests/test-issue-1935-session-limit-429.mjs` (15 assertions):
- session + weekly limits are detected as usage limits and are **not** transient-retryable;
- reset time / timezone extracted correctly;
- the `"hit your <window> limit"` backstop;
- regression guard the other way — the genuine transient #1924 429 **stays** retryable;
- a simulation of the exact `claude.lib.mjs` guard decision.

Existing suites stay green: `test-issue-1924-rate-limit-retry.mjs` (18), `test-usage-limit.mjs` (78), full default suite.

## Case study

[`docs/case-studies/issue-1935/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-1935-c4011ebdc787/docs/case-studies/issue-1935) — timeline, requirements table, blame history, root-cause analysis, fix, and online references. Raw logs archived under `data/`.

Closes #1935
title: fix(retry): treat session/weekly usage-limit 429s as account limits, not transient throttles (#1935)

body:
## Summary

Implements automatic continuation when Claude's usage limit resets, addressing issue #5.

When Claude outputs a message like `"⎿ 5-hour limit reached ∙ resets 5:30am"`, the script can now:

- **Detect** the limit reached message and parse the reset time
- **Wait** until the specified reset time with countdown logging  
- **Auto-resume** the same session with all original parameters

## Key Features

### New `--auto-continue-limit` / `-c` Flag

```bash
# Enable auto-continue to wait until limit resets
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" --auto-continue-limit

# Works with resume sessions too
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" --resume session-id --auto-continue-limit
```

### Enhanced Limit Detection

- Improved regex pattern catches variations like:
  - `"5-hour limit reached ∙ resets 5:30am"`  
  - `"24-hour limit reached • resets 11:45pm"`
  - `"Your 5-hour limit reached and resets 2:15pm"`
- Parses reset time in 12-hour format (5:30am, 11:45pm, etc.)
- Calculates exact wait time until next occurrence

### Smart Wait Logic

- **Countdown logging**: Shows remaining time at regular intervals
- **Time parsing**: Handles AM/PM formats and timezone-agnostic waiting
- **Auto-resume**: Reconstructs original command with all flags
- **Directory preservation**: Keeps working directory for seamless continuation

## Compatibility with Main Branch

- **Merged with latest main**: Includes all new features from main branch
- **Renamed flag**: Changed from `--auto-continue` to `--auto-continue-limit` to avoid conflicts
- **Preserves existing features**: The existing `--auto-continue` functionality (for PR continuation) is preserved
- **Comprehensive testing**: Added test scripts for both functionalities

## Usage Examples

**Basic auto-continue-limit:**
```bash
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" --auto-continue-limit
```

**With additional options:**
```bash  
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" \
  --auto-continue-limit \
  --model opus \
  --verbose \
  --fork
```

**Resume with auto-continue-limit:**
```bash
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" \
  --resume abc123-session-id \
  --auto-continue-limit
```

**Both auto-continue features:**
```bash
./solve.mjs "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123" \
  --auto-continue \          # Continue existing PRs older than 24h
  --auto-continue-limit      # Wait for Claude limit resets
```

## Implementation Details

- **Time parsing**: Robust parser handles 12-hour format with AM/PM
- **Wait calculation**: Schedules for next day if reset time already passed today  
- **Process spawning**: Uses child_process.spawn for clean session handoff
- **Cleanup prevention**: Preserves temp directory when auto-continue is active
- **Parameter preservation**: Maintains all original command flags through resume

## Test Plan

- [x] Time parsing for various formats (5:30am, 11:45pm, 12:00am, etc.)
- [x] Limit detection regex matches expected patterns
- [x] Help command shows new --auto-continue-limit option
- [x] Script runs without syntax errors
- [x] Examples demonstrate functionality
- [x] Merge conflicts resolved with main branch
- [x] Both auto-continue features work independently

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

---

Resolves #5
title: Auto continue when Claude limit resets
